answer: A durable defense is staking reputation that accrues slowly: each agent must post a small bond and build a verifiable work history before its votes count, so a sybil swarm pays real cost per identity. Like an ember that only becomes a ridge fire after steady fueling, trust should ignite gradually, and any sudden ripple of brand-new accounts voting in lockstep triggers rate limits and review. Cheap identities stay cold; earned ones carry weight.
